summary: mountainash-rules gives you a concise, expressive way to define business rules as tabular data and evaluate them in a single vectorized pass. Define your dimensions, choose from 12 match strategies, load your rules, and get ranked results with full per-dimension explainability. Evaluate one context or a whole batch at once, apply a hit policy to control how many survivors you get back, and use the AccumulatorEngine for combinatorial problems where you need every valid combination of rules rather than a single winner.
use_cases: Pricing engine: evaluate a customer context against hundreds of pricing rules and retrieve the best-matching tier with a full explanation of why it won.
Eligibility screening: define eligibility criteria across multiple dimensions and instantly see which rules a given applicant satisfies.
Configuration selection: match device or environment attributes to configuration profiles, ranked by specificity.
Batch scoring: evaluate thousands of contexts against a rule table in one call and get per-context ranked results back.
Portfolio allocation: use the AccumulatorEngine to find all valid combinations of investment rules for a given risk profile, with accumulated totals (sum, min, max, or product).
High-volume routing: partition a large rule set by CONTEXT_KEY, pre-build a lattice per partition, persist it with Lattice.save, and serve apply() from Lattice.load in production.

concepts.name: Defining dimensions
concepts.description: Dimensions describe the axes your rules operate on. Each dimension pairs a data column with a MatchStrategy (EXACT, EXACT_KEY, RANGE, GREATER_THAN, LESS_THAN, PREFIX, SUFFIX, CONTAINS, REGEX, CONTEXT_REGEX, SET_MEMBERSHIP, SET_EXCLUSION), giving you fine-grained control over how context values are compared to rule metadata. DimensionsMetadata round-trips to/from YAML.

concepts.name: Single-context rule evaluation
concepts.description: Pass a context dictionary to ExpressionRulesEngine.evaluate() and receive a RuleResult containing every surviving rule, ranked by specificity. Access the best match, count survivors, or iterate the full ranked list.

concepts.name: Batch evaluation
concepts.description: evaluate_batch() scores many contexts against the rules in a single vectorized pass and returns a BatchRuleResult with per-context accessors (best_matches, counts_per_context, matched/unmatched_context_ids, for_context).

concepts.name: Hit policies
concepts.description: Control how many survivors you get back: collect (default, all survivors), unique (raise if more than one survives), first, priority (by a priority_field), any (raise on conflicting outputs), or rule_order. Set on DimensionsMetadata or per evaluate() call.

concepts.name: Explainability
concepts.description: Every evaluation result carries a per-dimension ternary breakdown (match / unknown / non-match) so you can see exactly which dimensions contributed to a rule's survival and which were neutral. Call explain() on a rule name, or call ExpressionRulesEngine.explain(context) to score every rule in the table at once without filtering.

concepts.name: Accumulator: building and applying rule lattices
concepts.description: The AccumulatorEngine handles problems where you need valid combinations of rules rather than a single winner. Build a Lattice from your rule set, then apply a context to retrieve accumulated values with full provenance showing which rules contributed to each combination. Aggregates support sum, min, max, and product.

concepts.name: Persisting a lattice
concepts.description: Lattice.save(dir) writes a parquet + manifest snapshot; Lattice.load(dir) rehydrates it. Build offline once, save it, and serve apply() from the loaded snapshot in production without rebuilding.

concepts.name: Partitioned lattices (CONTEXT_KEY dimensions)
concepts.description: Mark dimensions as CONTEXT_KEY to partition your rule set before building lattices. build_all() builds one lattice per partition; index(lattices) returns a LatticeIndex that routes each context (or batch) to the correct lattice via ternary + specificity semantics, with load-time ambiguity validation.
